title: Sell Mineral Rights in Jensen, UT
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Jensen, UT | Uintah County
metaDescription: Own mineral or royalty interests near Jensen, Utah, along the Green River? Get a written offer built from your actual production data, no obligation.
heroLead: Jensen sits where the Green River crosses into eastern Uintah County near Dinosaur National Monument, on a stretch of the basin defined as much by its river-cut geology as by its wells.
intro: Jensen is a small community along US-40 near the confluence of the Green and Yampa Rivers, close to Dinosaur National Monument, and mineral ownership in the area reflects the mix of ranching homesteads and oil and gas leasing that has shaped eastern Uintah County for the better part of a century. Wells here tie into the broader Uinta Basin trend, generally on the flank rather than in a specific named core field.
If your family holds a mineral interest near Jensen, we will confirm the legal description and production history against Utah Division of Oil, Gas and Mining records before making a written offer.

sections.heading: Ranching homesteads and long-held minerals
paragraphs: Much of the land around Jensen was originally settled for ranching, and the mineral estate frequently stayed with the family even as the surface changed hands or was leased out for grazing over the decades. It is common to find an interest here that has never been actively managed — no one in the family has called the operator, checked the division order against current ownership, or considered what the interest might be worth outright, because the royalty checks, however modest, simply kept arriving.

sections.heading: Proximity to the national monument and land use overlap
paragraphs: Because Jensen sits close to Dinosaur National Monument, some nearby acreage falls under different surface-use restrictions than land further from the park boundary, even where the mineral estate itself is privately owned and unaffected by park status. We check this as part of confirming your interest, since surface access considerations can occasionally affect how and when an operator can develop a unit, which in turn factors into a fair valuation.

faqs.question: Does being near Dinosaur National Monument affect my mineral rights?
faqs.answer: Generally not the ownership itself, but it can affect surface access and development timing in some cases, which we check as part of confirming your interest.

faqs.question: My family has never actively managed this interest. Where do we start?
faqs.answer: Send us whatever deed or division order paperwork you have, and we will confirm the legal description and current status for you.

faqs.question: Is the acreage near Jensen part of a specific named field?
faqs.answer: Not typically — it generally sits on the flank of the broader Uinta Basin trend rather than in a single named core field.
